claims.title: Johnston told to destroy first-generation Apollo negatives
claims.claim: Ken Johnston Sr. says he was told to destroy a batch of first-generation Apollo negatives because they had anomalies on them that "they don't want to release publicly" / "aren't supposed to be there."
claims.rationale: destruction order plausible but single-source; the 'first-generation negatives' and censorship-motive framing are unsupported (see findings/ken-johnston.md)

claims.title: Johnston's NASA role
claims.claim: Ken Johnston Sr. was a pilot who trained NASA astronauts and was a backup astronaut for the Apollo missions.
claims.rationale: never an astronaut or NASA employee; rejected from the 1977 astronaut selection (see findings/ken-johnston.md)

claims.title: Johnston saved negatives and posted them
claims.claim: Johnston saved some of the negatives and put copies of them online.
claims.rationale: he kept a set of prints and posted copies to the Internet Archive (see findings/ken-johnston.md)

claims.title: Saved copies publicly available
claims.claim: These saved copies are publicly available in an archive.
claims.rationale: the archive is publicly available online (see findings/ken-johnston.md)

claims.title: Copies are early-generation
claims.claim: Johnston says the saved copies are early-generation copies of the very original photographs.
claims.rationale: they were 8x10 prints, not established as early-generation, and the originals still exist at JSC (see findings/ken-johnston.md)

claims.title: Other public copies differ
claims.claim: Most of the publicly available copies elsewhere have differences compared to Johnston's copies.
claims.rationale: differences best explained by scanner contamination plus brightness-pushing, not censorship (see findings/ken-johnston.md)

claims.title: "March to the Moon" archive
claims.claim: There is a NASA archive called "March to the Moon," said to be the latest scans of NASA's original Apollo mission films.
claims.rationale: 'March to the Moon' is a real JSC/ASU rescan project (see findings/ken-johnston.md)

claims.title: Cross-archive inconsistencies
claims.claim: Comparing "March to the Moon" scans with Johnston's copies and with scans from other NASA branches reveals "a lot of... obvious inconsistencies."

claims.title: Lights blacked out in some scans, not others
claims.claim: Lights or UAP-type structures are clearly blacked out in some NASA-scanned versions but not others for the same frames — "provable inconsistencies across... different NASA archives... for the same frames."
claims.rationale: no redaction; the frame's second, brighter blue anomaly survives the same LPI shadow-clip (see findings/AS14-66-9301/FINDING.md)

claims.title: LPI Apollo 14 frame of Ed Mitchell
claims.claim: A scan from the Lunar and Planetary Institute (LPI) archive (NASA-managed since the 1970s) shows an Apollo 14 photograph of Ed Mitchell standing on the lunar surface with a long shadow.
claims.rationale: the frame is real (LPI Apollo Image Atlas) (see findings/AS14-66-9301/FINDING.md)

claims.title: LPI version: black sky
claims.claim: In the LPI version of that frame the lunar sky is completely black, even zoomed in everywhere.
claims.rationale: true for the print-res LPI file, whose sky is globally clipped to black (see findings/AS14-66-9301/FINDING.md)

claims.title: "March to the Moon A" version: blue orb visible
claims.claim: In the "March to the Moon A" version of the same frame (managed by Johnson Space Center and Arizona State University) there is a blue orb clearly visible in the lunar sky above Mitchell.
claims.rationale: the blue orb is present in the March-to-the-Moon and other high-res scans (see findings/AS14-66-9301/FINDING.md)

claims.title: Brightened LPI frame shows a cutout
claims.claim: Brightening the LPI version reveals a blackish cutout/discoloration in the exact spot where the blue orb appears in the March to the Moon version.
claims.rationale: no cutout or patch boundary; the sky is uniform digital zero plus JPEG speckle (see findings/AS14-66-9301/FINDING.md)

claims.title: Brightened LPI frame shows other anomalies
claims.claim: The brightened LPI frame also shows a "mushroom-like cloud" light anomaly and bright streaks in the otherwise black lunar sky.
claims.rationale: brightening a clipped-to-zero sky yields only speckle, not real mushroom-cloud/streak anomalies (see findings/AS14-66-9301/FINDING.md)

claims.title: Many other archive discrepancies
claims.claim: Derakhshani has found "many other examples" of this sort of discrepancy examining different archives.

claims.title: Bluish insectoid streaks on negatives
claims.claim: On the negatives you can see "bluish metallic-looking streaks that are very bright in a certain area," which under zoom "almost looks like an insectoid-type probe-like metallic object."
claims.rationale: quote verified at [0:00:07]; the 'insectoid probe' features are film scratches/emulsion defects amplified by pixel clipping (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Johnston's relay of Mitchell's blue orbs
claims.claim: Ken Johnston says Ed Mitchell confessed to him that they "saw these blue orb-like lights following us... from the lunar surface."
claims.rationale: blue-orbs reach the public only via Johnston/Coulthart, never from Mitchell on record; contradicted by C107 (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Additional Apollo 17 anomalies beyond the released trio
claims.claim: Derakhshani has found UAP-type anomalies in Apollo 17 photographs beyond the trio of blue lights released in the first tranche.
claims.rationale: Derakhshani said it at [0:18:51]; no genuine non-artifact UAPs exist on the additional frames (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Self-discovered, made public a year prior
claims.claim: Derakhshani discovered these additional Apollo 17 anomalies himself over a year before the interview and made them public in certain forums.
claims.rationale: accurate self-description of his prior online anomaly-forum postings (2022–2023) (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Frame AS-17-147-22470, trio of blue lights
claims.claim: Apollo 17 frame "AS-17-147-22470," taken from the lunar surface, shows a lunar hill with, above and to the left in the black sky, three solid-looking blue lights nearly equidistant from each other.
claims.rationale: the trio is real on the scans, but debunked as an object (absent from adjacent frames 22469/22471) (see findings/AS17-147-22470/FINDING.md)

claims.title: Raw scan publicly available
claims.claim: A raw digital scan of Apollo 17 frame AS-17-147-22470 is publicly available.
claims.rationale: raw ASU/Flickr/JSC scans are publicly available (see findings/AS17-147-22470/FINDING.md)

claims.title: Inter-light brightening suggests one object
claims.claim: Brightening/increasing exposure shows the region between the three lights becomes significantly brighter than the rest of the sky, suggesting they may be attached to a single object rather than three independent lights.
claims.rationale: persistence test: the trio exists only on frame 22470, consistent with an emulsion defect, not one object (see findings/AS17-147-22470/FINDING.md)

claims.title: NASA/DoW opened a special investigation
claims.claim: When NASA released this image in the first tranche, the description stated the Department of War and NASA opened a special investigation because preliminary analysis suggested the lights are "probably part of a physical object."
claims.rationale: with corrections - the PURSUE caption says it in substance, but it was a Department of War release, says 'potentially' not 'probably,' and never names the frame (see findings/loose-ends.md)

claims.title: NASA acquired the original film
claims.claim: NASA said in that description that they acquired the original film from Apollo 17 for this image and would analyze it and report results.
claims.rationale: attribution loose - the caption says 'the government' obtained the original film and promises the NASA/DoW analysis results (see findings/loose-ends.md)

claims.title: More unreleased anomalies exist
claims.claim: There are more, "even more impressive" UAP anomalies from Apollo 17 and earlier Apollo missions, taken from the lunar surface, that NASA has not released in the last two tranches.
claims.rationale: quote verified at [0:19:18]; all Apollo 70mm film has long been publicly digitized, no secret objects on unreleased tranches (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Isaacman may be unaware of them
claims.claim: Derakhshani is not sure Administrator Isaacman is even aware of these additional unreleased images.
claims.rationale: personal speculation about the administrator's knowledge; inherently untestable (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Second Apollo 17 photo: rover tracks + insectoid object
claims.claim: A second Apollo 17 photograph (frame number not recalled) shows lunar rover tracks and, in the black sky, bluish metallic streaks that under brightening look like an "insectoid type probe-like metallic bluish metallic object."
claims.rationale: frame AS17-137-20925 is real (rover tracks + blue streak); the 'insectoid probe' is a film defect plus exposure-pushing artifact (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Photographer was Cernan or Schmitt
claims.claim: That image was probably photographed by either Eugene Cernan or Harrison Schmitt, since they were the only two on the lunar surface during Apollo 17.
claims.rationale: Cernan and Schmitt were the only Apollo 17 surface crew, so one of them took it (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: NASA has not released this image
claims.claim: NASA has not released this particular Apollo 17 image.
claims.rationale: the frame was not in NASA's official UAP tranches, though public in standard JSC catalogs (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Second enveloped object with debris tail
claims.claim: In that same image there is a similar second object just above the first with a similar "enveloping" brightening effect and a contrail / "debris tail."
claims.rationale: the 'envelope' and 'debris tail' are scan-noise halos and JPEG line bleeding from extreme exposure pushing (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Similar object ~8 frames later
claims.claim: About eight frames later in the same image sequence, a similar metallic-looking object with an envelope and trail appears in the lunar sky.
claims.rationale: a blemish exists on AS17-137-20933 ~8 frames later, but the craft interpretation is a recurring roll defect (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Elapsed time between frames unknown
claims.claim: The elapsed time between these frames is unknown.
claims.rationale: timestamps aren't printed on film, but frame timing is reconstructible to seconds from ALSJ voice logs (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Images sit uncommented in NASA public archives
claims.claim: These images "are all there in NASA's public image archives," and NASA does not comment on them within the archives.
claims.rationale: JSC EOL and LPI host the raw images with standard metadata and no UAP commentary (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Loeb: cosmic rays as most likely explanation
claims.claim: Avi Loeb has suggested cosmic rays hitting the film as the most likely explanation for the trio of blue lights in the Apollo 17 image.
claims.rationale: verified verbatim in Avi Loeb's May 18 2026 Medium post (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Tyson debunked, "case closed"
claims.claim: Neil deGrasse Tyson publicly debunked the Apollo 17 sightings, citing cosmic rays as "case closed."
claims.rationale: Tyson publicly cited cosmic-ray/particle hits in May 2026 StarTalk/TikTok videos (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Cosmic rays on sensors make thin streaks
claims.claim: Cosmic rays hitting digital camera sensors typically produce thin, long streaks because they usually enter at an angle rather than perpendicular.
claims.rationale: oblique cosmic rays streak, but normal-incidence hits make 1–4 pixel round dots, and Apollo used film not CCDs (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: NASA's own cosmic-ray examples show streaks, not dots
claims.claim: NASA has produced its own documented examples of cosmic-ray artifacts in digital images showing thin, long streaks, not solid bluish dots.
claims.rationale: NASA/STScI documentation records both linear tracks and point/dot clusters from cosmic rays (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Radiation on film causes fogging, not seen here
claims.claim: Radiation striking film tends to produce a fogging effect, which is not observed in the Apollo 17 frames in question.
claims.rationale: high-energy heavy-ion cosmic particles leave sharp localized micro-spots on film without general fogging (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Similar trio in an Apollo 11 frame
claims.claim: A similar trio of lights (like the Apollo 17 case) also appears in an Apollo 11 frame.
claims.rationale: frame AS11-40-5903 shows a similar spot cluster, confirmed to be internal Hasselblad lens flares (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Mitchell: aliens followed "all the way"
claims.claim: Edgar Mitchell (Apollo 14) privately told somebody that there were aliens following them "all the way."
claims.rationale: no on-record Mitchell statement; third-hand hearsay (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Coulthart's "In Plain Sight" discusses Mitchell
claims.claim: Ross Coulthart's book, which Derakhshani believes is called "In Plain Sight," discusses Mitchell's lunar experience.
claims.rationale: Coulthart's 2021 In Plain Sight devotes Chapter 20 to Edgar Mitchell (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: "The spaceman" anonymous source
claims.claim: Coulthart quotes an anonymous source called "the spaceman," who was very close personal friends with Ed Mitchell.
claims.rationale: Coulthart uses the pseudonym 'The Spaceman' for an anonymous close contact of Mitchell (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Spaceman's relay of Mitchell's blue orbs
claims.claim: The "spaceman" source says Mitchell confessed "we saw these blue orb-like lights following us" from the lunar surface, flying around above the lunar sky.
claims.rationale: reaches the public only via Coulthart's anonymous 'spaceman', never from Mitchell (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Mitchell: not camera artifacts
claims.claim: Mitchell reportedly said he wasn't sure if the lights were extraterrestrial in origin, but they definitely saw them and they're "not camera artifacts."
claims.rationale: attributed to Mitchell but not in any on-record statement (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: "Simpkinsin" (sp?) archive photo
claims.claim: There is a NASA-archive UFO photo referred to as "Simpkinsin" (sp?), recommended to Michels by Chris Ramsey.
claims.rationale: refers to the Scott H. Simpkinson archive lithograph of the Gemini XI object (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Believed to be from the Gemini 11 archive
claims.claim: Michels believes this is a real photo of something from the Gemini 11 archive.
claims.rationale: the document concerns the Gemini 11 mission (September 1966) (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Gemini 11 power outage
claims.claim: There was a power outage during Gemini 11, with audio associated with the event.
claims.rationale: the Gemini XI Mission Report documents the visual-object sighting and a power-bus transient (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Michels thinks the Gemini 11 photo is airbrushed
claims.claim: Michels thinks the Gemini 11 photo "was airbrushed on" and is not a real photo, reasoning that otherwise it would be "the best photo of all time."
claims.rationale: Michels said it; the lithograph is an artist composite/briefing aid, not a raw photo (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Michels spoke to Knuth about Gemini 11
claims.claim: Michels spoke to Kevin Knuth about the Gemini 11 incident.
claims.rationale: Michels interviewed Dr. Kevin Knuth on record about Gemini-era UAP reports (see findings/wave3/photo-remainder.md)

claims.title: Aldrin knows more than he can say
claims.claim: Buzz Aldrin "probably knows more than he can say" about UFOs/UAP.

claims.title: Mitchell knew more than he could say
claims.claim: Edgar Mitchell "probably knew more than he could say" about UFOs/UAP.
claims.rationale: 'knew more than he could say' is unfalsifiable; on record he attributed everything to others' testimony (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Armstrong "told not to come back to the Moon"
claims.claim: Neil Armstrong was overheard (per apocryphal stories, at a party in Washington, DC with "bigwigs") saying "we were told not to come back to the Moon"; several people say he said it.
claims.rationale: apocryphal Timothy Good-style UFO lore; Armstrong's real quote is the mundane flashing-lights explanation (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Pete Worden knows more about NASA/UAP
claims.claim: Pete Worden (at NASA) allegedly knows a lot more about NASA's knowledge of the UFO phenomenon and astronauts' observations of anomalies in space.

claims.title: Worden's NASA position
claims.claim: Pete Worden held a "fairly high" associate-administrator-type position at NASA (exact title not recalled).

claims.title: Worden connected DeLonge and McCaslin
claims.claim: Pete Worden connected Tom DeLonge and General Neil McCaslin ("public information").

claims.title: Worden and the Breakthrough Prize
claims.claim: Pete Worden was involved as an administrator in the Breakthrough Prize (related to exotic signals in space).

claims.title: Worden moved to Luxembourg
claims.claim: Pete Worden moved to Luxembourg after his NASA/Breakthrough work.

claims.title: Worden's "very strange" book
claims.claim: Pete Worden wrote a book in the early 2000s that Michels ordered and found "very strange."

claims.title: Dan Goldin suspected of knowing more
claims.claim: Dan Goldin is suspected of knowing more about NASA/UAP matters.

claims.title: Bill Nelson suspected of knowing more
claims.claim: Bill Nelson is suspected of knowing more about NASA/UAP matters.

claims.title: Harrison Schmitt suspected of knowing more
claims.claim: Dr. Harrison Schmitt (Apollo 17, one of the last men on the Moon with Eugene Cernan) is suspected of knowing more; Schmitt is alive as of this recording.

claims.title: Schmitt never commented on file drops
claims.claim: Harrison Schmitt has never commented on any of the NASA UAP file drops.

claims.title: Aldrin admitted something followed Apollo 11
claims.claim: Buzz Aldrin has admitted in multiple interviews that something was following the Apollo 11 spacecraft.
claims.rationale: Aldrin says an object was visible; his own explanation is a sunlit jettisoned SLA panel (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Aldrin went back to sleep, didn't report it
claims.claim: Aldrin said he went back to sleep and did not report the object because the crew would have "been looked at as sort of ridiculous."
claims.rationale: matches Aldrin's own account of not reporting it to avoid a flying-saucer frenzy (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Apollo 11 crew member describes moving illumination
claims.claim: An Apollo 11 crew member describes seeing "illumination that was moving with respect to the stars" and that they avoided reporting it to Houston, "technically... an unidentified flying object."

claims.title: Aldrin's later S-IVB explanation (Larry King Live)
claims.claim: In a subsequent interview (Larry King Live, circa 2007, with James Fox and Stanton Friedman present), Aldrin said he was "now almost certain" the object was a panel from the S-IVB (S4B) rocket booster that broke off and moved along with the capsule.
claims.rationale: Larry King 2007 panel explanation verified from the CNN transcript (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: S-IVB booster reportedly 6,000 miles away
claims.claim: The S-IVB booster was reportedly 6,000 miles away from the capsule at the time.
claims.rationale: the booster was maneuvered away, which is why Aldrin concludes it was a panel (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Panel drifted alongside capsule for days
claims.claim: Aldrin's proposed explanation is that a panel from the booster got free and drifted alongside the Apollo capsule for multiple days en route to the Moon.
claims.rationale: accurately attributes Aldrin's own stated panel explanation (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Aldrin's sister on his two sightings
claims.claim: Faye Ann Potter, Buzz Aldrin's sister, told James Fox that Aldrin had two UFO sightings — one on Apollo 11 and one over Japan as a fighter pilot/test pilot.

claims.title: Fox pursued Aldrin around the world
claims.claim: James Fox pursued Buzz Aldrin around the world (including to Monte Carlo) trying to get a statement on UFOs.

claims.title: "What would my testimony do anyways?"
claims.claim: At the last minute before an interview in Monte Carlo, Aldrin reportedly said, "What would my testimony do anyways?"

claims.title: Aldrin cites reputational risk (Paul Allen / SETI)
claims.claim: A statement attributed to Aldrin references Paul Allen investing in SETI and being labeled "a UFO freak," and says "I can't jeopardize my initiative... I'm working with Congress right now... to develop a rocket that's gonna help put civilians into space."

claims.title: Paul Allen backed SETI, criticized for it
claims.claim: Paul Allen (Microsoft co-founder) backed SETI and received criticism for it.

claims.title: "How's my story gonna change anything anyway?"
claims.claim: Aldrin said, in effect, "How's my story gonna change anything anyway?"

claims.title: Derakhshani approached Aldrin via Buzz Aldrin Ventures
claims.claim: Derakhshani tried to approach Buzz Aldrin through an assistant at Buzz Aldrin Ventures to show him Apollo 11 and Apollo 17 UAP imagery.

claims.title: Aldrin "not available" to review images
claims.claim: Derakhshani received a polite reply saying Aldrin is not available to review or analyze the images.

claims.title: Same unavailability applies to Schmitt
claims.claim: The same unavailability applies to Harrison Schmitt regarding looking at the imagery or discussing it publicly.

claims.title: Embarrassment then mockery on Larry King
claims.claim: An unnamed person was visibly embarrassed on Larry King's show and then resorted to mockery.

claims.title: The Criss Angel deflection
claims.claim: That person said (paraphrased/quoted), "Well, you guys saw Criss Angel last night at a show. How much of what he did could you not explain?"

claims.title: Derakhshani couldn't explain Criss Angel either
claims.claim: Derakhshani says he personally could not explain anything Criss Angel did.

claims.title: Jausen was friends with Cernan
claims.claim: Takanobu Jausen (sp?) was personal friends with Apollo 17 astronaut Eugene Cernan.
claims.rationale: Takano-Cernan acquaintance is well-supported (museum holds Cernan's flight garment) (see findings/photo-whistleblowers.md)

claims.title: Cernan's telepathic "we don't want you here"
claims.claim: Jausen said Cernan told him that on the way to the Moon during Apollo 17, Cernan received a telepathic message saying "We don't really want you here."
claims.rationale: sole source is Takano; Cernan never said it on record and was a public skeptic (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: "I was told never to come back"
claims.claim: "So then, well, his answer was, 'I was told never to come back.'"
claims.rationale: same single-source telepathy story, uncorroborated (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: "It came directly to my brain"
claims.claim: "Yeah. Well, this isn't an earphone. It came directly to my brain."
claims.rationale: same single-source telepathy story, uncorroborated (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Mitchell's mystical / conversion experience
claims.claim: Mitchell had a publicly discussed telepathic/parapsychological "mystical"/"conversion" experience in which his whole worldview updated on the way back from the Moon.
claims.rationale: Mitchell's mystical/samadhi experience is real and self-described (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Mitchell's public Roswell / legacy-program beliefs
claims.claim: Publicly, Mitchell was clear he believed an extraterrestrial spacecraft crashed at Roswell, that the government recovered it, and that there is a legacy secret UFO reverse-engineering program.
claims.rationale: Mitchell publicly and repeatedly stated his Roswell/legacy-program beliefs (second-hand) (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Mitchell: never saw a UFO on his missions
claims.claim: Publicly, Mitchell said he himself never saw anything on any of his missions that would count as a UFO.
claims.rationale: Mitchell said on record he never personally saw a UFO on his missions (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Mitchell–Hoagland Coast to Coast AM debate
claims.claim: Mitchell and Richard Hoagland had a long debate on Art Bell's Coast to Coast AM show in the 1990s.
claims.rationale: the Mitchell-Hoagland Coast to Coast AM debate is real and archived (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Debate available on Rumble
claims.claim: That debate is available on Rumble ("I think").

claims.title: Mitchell dismissive of Hoagland's lunar structures
claims.claim: In that debate, Mitchell was very skeptical and even dismissive of Hoagland's ideas about possible glass-like structures or debris on/above the lunar surface.
claims.rationale: in that debate Mitchell was dismissive of Hoagland's lunar-structure claims (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Borman downplayed his Gemini 7 sighting
claims.claim: Frank Borman downplayed his Gemini 7 sighting for the rest of his life, as did other astronauts with their own sightings.
claims.rationale: event real, but 'downplayed = hid an anomaly' is unsupported; the crew endorsed the booster-debris reconstruction (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: Early astronauts were Freemasons
claims.claim: Many/almost all early astronauts, including John Glenn, were Freemasons ("They were all Freemasons").
claims.rationale: ~8 of 73 astronauts have documented lodge records; Armstrong never a Mason, Glenn not until 1978 (see findings/freemasons.md)

claims.title: Hoagland's "Dark Mission"
claims.claim: Michels wants to discuss Richard Hoagland's book "Dark Mission."
claims.rationale: Dark Mission (Feral House, 2007) exists (see findings/freemasons.md)

claims.title: Occult rituals, Launchpad 33, equinox timing
claims.claim: Hoagland's material asserts there were occult rituals connected to the space program, referencing "Launchpad 33" and launches timed to equinoxes for success.
claims.rationale: the book verbatim asserts rituals/33/stellar timing; the asserted content itself is debunked (see findings/freemasons.md)

claims.title: Pasulka: second-century Latin on Apollo rockets
claims.claim: Diana Pasulka has said second-century Latin was inscribed on some of the Apollo missions' rockets.
claims.rationale: no transcript of Pasulka saying it was located (see findings/freemasons.md)

claims.title: Aldrin a 33rd-degree Scottish Rite Freemason
claims.claim: Buzz Aldrin states in one of his own books that he is a 33rd-degree Scottish Rite Freemason.
claims.rationale: Aldrin a confirmed Mason and the Supreme Council styles him 33°, but no such passage found in his own books (see findings/freemasons.md)

claims.title: Aldrin's Masonic communion on the Moon
claims.claim: Buzz Aldrin performed a communion that was a Masonic ritual on the Moon.
claims.rationale: the communion was Presbyterian per Aldrin's own 1970 first-person account; Masonic reading exists only in Dark Mission (see findings/freemasons.md)

claims.title: Disproportionate Freemasonry among Apollo-era personnel
claims.claim: A disproportionately large number of astronauts and NASA engineers during the Apollo era were Freemasons.
claims.rationale: 11-14% observed vs ~8% national male base rate in Masonry's peak era (see findings/freemasons.md)

claims.title: Johnston himself a 33rd-degree Freemason
claims.claim: Ken Johnston Sr. is apparently himself a 33rd-degree Freemason.
claims.rationale: no documentation located either way on Johnston's Freemasonry (see findings/ken-johnston.md)

claims.title: Astronaut Freemasonry anomalous for the era
claims.claim: Early astronauts being Freemasons was anomalous even for that era, unlike broader elite American society membership (e.g., compared to the Founding Fathers era).
claims.rationale: the era was the statistical zenith of American Freemasonry (peak 1957-59) (see findings/freemasons.md)

claims.title: von Braun / Disney "33" cartoon
claims.claim: Wernher von Braun and Walt Disney made a Disney cartoon movie around the space age featuring "thirty-three" as a recurring symbol.
claims.rationale: films real, but '33' is a single dialogue line per the claim's own root source, and Disney was never a Mason (see findings/freemasons.md)

claims.title: There was a "Launchpad 33"
claims.claim: There was a "Launchpad 33."
claims.rationale: White Sands LC-33 exists but was originally Army Launch Area No. 1, one of many numbered pads (see findings/freemasons.md)

claims.title: 1992 Brookhaven UFO crash/recovery
claims.claim: There was a UFO crash in 1992 near Brookhaven National Labs, in a town he calls "Southaven," where residents allegedly saw National Labs staff recover and take the craft into the labs.

claims.title: Spergel on/chairing 2022 NASA UAP panel
claims.claim: David Spergel, head of the Simons Science Foundation, was on the NASA UAP review panel in 2022, and was "kind of chairing it."

claims.title: NASA/DoD legally linked since the Space Act of 1958
claims.claim: NASA and DoD have been tightly linked in law since the Space Act of 1958, which created NASA via Congressional act.
claims.rationale: a real NASA-DoD legal linkage exists but 'tightly linked' overstates it; NASA is a civilian agency (see findings/documents-statutes.md)

claims.title: Space Act: DoD oversight, national-security missions

claims.claim: Either Brandenburg, or possibly Michels' friend "Science Bob McGuire," was in a meeting with the top scientist on Venus about an anomaly there, and Carl Sagan was in that meeting along with a White House science advisor.

claims.title: "Carl Sagan was sitting in the room."
claims.claim: "Carl Sagan was sitting in the room."

claims.title: Sagan's "contractor green badge"
claims.claim: Sagan "had a contractor green badge with a picture on it. You don't get that if you're casual."

claims.title: Menzel caught destroying astronomical plates
claims.claim: Don Menzel was "caught destroying astronomical plates" by an assistant, an astronomer in her own right at Harvard, named Dorit Hofleit (sp?).
claims.rationale: Hoffleit did document committee-voted plate destruction under Menzel; 'caught destroying' is dramatization (see findings/sagan.md)

claims.title: Sagan attributed sightings to weather/inversions

claims.title: Sagan interested in directed panspermia
claims.claim: Carl Sagan was very interested in directed panspermia.
claims.rationale: panspermia writings and Crick-Orgel engagement documented; no strong personal-interest statement verified (see findings/sagan.md)

claims.title: Brandenburg's credentials
claims.claim: John Brandenburg has a physics PhD and worked at Sandia (national labs) for a lot of his career.
claims.rationale: UC Davis plasma-physics PhD; Sandia was one Reagan-era stint, not his whole career (see findings/clementine-brandenburg.md)

claims.title: Brandenburg on ancient Mars structures / Cydonia
claims.claim: Brandenburg theorized about ancient structures on Mars, including at Cydonia.

claims.title: Hoagland also reports on Cydonia

claims.rationale: Hoagland has covered Cydonia for decades (Monuments of Mars, enterprisemission.org) (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Recent "square object" on Mars

claims.title: Brandenburg: argon-40/xenon-129 excess → Mars nuclear holocaust
claims.claim: Brandenburg claimed argon-40 and xenon-129 exist on Mars in excess of what would be expected from natural radioactive isotope decay, implying a past nuclear holocaust on Mars.
claims.rationale: accurately reports his argument; the nuclear-holocaust conclusion is unsupported/debunked (Xe-129 is radiogenic) (see findings/clementine-brandenburg.md)

claims.title: Aldrin friends with Arthur C. Clarke
claims.claim: Buzz Aldrin was friends with science fiction author Arthur C. Clarke.

claims.title: Kubrick's "2001" based on Clarke's books
claims.claim: Stanley Kubrick made "2001: A Space Odyssey" based on Arthur C. Clarke's books.
claims.rationale: 2001 built from Clarke's 'The Sentinel,' novel/screenplay co-developed with Kubrick (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Clarke lived in Sri Lanka, wrote of a "portal"
claims.claim: Arthur C. Clarke lived in Sri Lanka and wrote a book about a "portal" in Sri Lanka.
claims.rationale: Sri Lanka residence confirmed; the 'portal' book is a garbled Fountains of Paradise (space elevator) (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: "Childhood's End" premise
claims.claim: Arthur C. Clarke wrote "Childhood's End," about an alien presence that infiltrates the highest ranks of government and speaks through non-verbal autistic children.
claims.rationale: book exists but premise misdescribed: Overlords arrive openly, no autistic children as channels (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Clarke's ~2000 Sri Lanka interview with Aldrin present
claims.claim: Arthur C. Clarke gave a media interview at his home in Sri Lanka circa 2000, during which Buzz Aldrin was visiting him.
claims.rationale: videotaped space.com chat at Clarke's home, Feb 25, 2001, Aldrin present (date off ~1 yr) (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Photograph of Clarke and Aldrin together
claims.claim: There exists a photograph of that media interview showing Clarke and Buzz Aldrin together.
claims.rationale: photo published with the space.com article (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Clarke: NASA "discovered large forms of life on Mars"
claims.claim: In that interview, Clarke, asked about Mars, said: "What's really shocking and exciting to me is that... NASA has basically discovered large forms of life on Mars. Have a look at the pictures of Mars from Jet Propulsion Laboratories... I don't see any other interpretation other than that these are gigantic forms of biological life on Mars."
claims.rationale: he said it, verbatim archived (type A); the content is debunked - CO2-geyser dune spots per HiRISE (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Aldrin did not contradict Clarke
claims.claim: In that interview, Buzz Aldrin sat there quietly and did not contradict or disagree with Clarke's Mars-life statement.
claims.rationale: 'Aldrin did not comment' per the contemporaneous article; silence is not agreement (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Derakhshani has seen the specific Mars images
claims.claim: Derakhshani has personally seen the specific Mars images that Clarke was referring to in that interview.
claims.rationale: private perceptual claim; the underlying MOC frames are public (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Clarke a proponent of studying the Face on Mars
claims.claim: Arthur C. Clarke was a proponent of studying the "Face on Mars" more closely and thought it was a promising candidate for an ET-built structure.
claims.rationale: no primary source found for Clarke championing the Face; his documented claims were vegetation-type (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: MGS/HiRISE: possible fossilized life or exotic tech
claims.claim: There are images from Mars Global Surveyor and (more recently) HiRISE showing formations that could resemble the skeletal structure of fossilized large life forms on Mars, or exotic technology.
claims.rationale: pareidolic interpretation via an AI-upscaling pipeline; no peer-reviewed support (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Derakhshani interviewed John Ward
claims.claim: Derakhshani recently conducted an interview with John Ward, described as a Mars anomalies researcher.
claims.rationale: the interview is real; the researcher is Jean (not John) Ward (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Ward's ruins/fungal Mars formations
claims.claim: John Ward has discovered anomalous formations/structures on Mars that look like ruins or fungal structures spanning hundreds of meters in area.
claims.rationale: Ward claims it (type A); the structures themselves are unsupported and pass through AI upscaling (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Fractal/texture algorithms imply non-natural origin
claims.claim: In the interview with John Ward, Derakhshani applied fractal and texture-based algorithms to evaluate whether the Mars formations could form naturally, and the algorithms imply the landforms are probably not of natural origin.
claims.rationale: interview covered Carlotto's artificiality processing; 'probably not natural' is a self-reported result from a method falsified on the Face (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Many similar HiRISE/MGS images exist
claims.claim: There are many other images of this type from NASA's own HiRISE and Mars Global Surveyor (MGS) missions of the Martian surface.
claims.rationale: trivially - the image archives are public; 'of this type' interpretation exists only in anomaly-hunter readings (see findings/mars.md)

claims.title: Aldrin insinuated the Phobos monolith worth visiting
claims.claim: Buzz Aldrin has insinuated that a "monolith" NASA has imaged on Phobos (a moon of Mars) is an interesting structure worth visiting and sampling.
claims.rationale: he said it, but explicitly declined the artificial-origin reading ('the universe put it there') (see findings/astronaut-testimony.md)

claims.title: NASA proposed a 2007 Phobos sample mission
claims.claim: NASA proposed a mission in 2007 to send a probe to the Phobos monolith to take a physical sample and perform direct analysis.
claims.rationale: real 2007 PRIME concept targeting the monolith, but Canadian Space Agency-selected, not NASA; never flew (see findings/phobos.md)

claims.title: Phobos monolith dimensions
claims.claim: The Phobos monolith is estimated to be about 85-90 meters in diameter and about 90 meters tall (roughly 270 feet).
claims.rationale: NASA's own caption says ~85 m diameter; the ~90 m height is a community shadow-analysis estimate (see findings/phobos.md)

claims.title: Derakhshani examined NASA's Phobos images
claims.claim: Derakhshani has personally examined NASA's images of the Phobos monolith.
claims.rationale: personal claim; the imagery is public and trivially viewable (see findings/phobos.md)

claims.title: No other structure on Phobos as large
claims.claim: There is no other structure anywhere else on Phobos nearly as large as this monolith, though smaller monoliths of similar type exist on Phobos.
claims.rationale: largest of several documented boulders (1-100 m DPRF population); no exhaustive survey exists (see findings/phobos.md)

claims.title: Monolith geologically anomalous
claims.claim: The Phobos monolith is geologically anomalous — it does not appear to be a natural formation, is "too large," "too symmetrical," and its albedo/reflectivity is significantly different from the rest of the Phobos surface.
claims.rationale: NASA describes a boulder among Stickney ejecta; brightness matches fresh ejecta; 'symmetry' is a pixel-resolution artifact (see findings/phobos.md)

claims.title: "Wishbone" structure on the far side
claims.claim: There is a "wishbone" structure on the far/back side of the Moon.
claims.rationale: no USGS/LROC/NASA source for a far-side 'wishbone'; zero search hits; likely a fringe name (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Any ET visitation was long ago
claims.claim: If the Moon was visited by extraterrestrials, it most likely happened a very long time ago (perhaps millions to billions of years ago).
claims.rationale: an if-then ET-timing speculation with no empirical content (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Structures would erode without atmosphere
claims.claim: The Moon has no atmosphere, so any built structures would be eroded/pulverized over time by micrometeoroid bombardment and eventually flattened, smoothed, or rounded.
claims.rationale: NASA MEO confirms micrometeoroid erosion since the Moon has no atmosphere to stop impacts (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Volcanic/tectonic activity long ceased
claims.claim: Volcanic activity on the Moon ceased roughly one to three billion years ago, and intrinsic tectonic activity has more or less stopped.
claims.rationale: with nuance - NASA: no erupting volcanoes today; peak volcanism 3.3–3.8 Ga, ceased ~1–1.5 Ga (minor young IMPs/Chang'e-5 basalts aside) (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Paracelsus C precise geometries
claims.claim: There are structures in "Paracelsus C," a crater on the far/back side of the Moon, that have "unusually precise geometries."
claims.rationale: the crater is real, but 'precise geometries' appear only in a non-peer-reviewed Carlotto 2016 JSE paper; pareidolia fits LRO morphology (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Derakhshani's lunar-ruins project
claims.claim: Derakhshani describes his own ongoing project: identifying geologically anomalous objects, structures, formations, and phenomena on the Moon as candidates for ancient, highly-eroded ruins.
claims.rationale: he describes the lunar-ruins project at [0:57:48] (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Next step: probe/rover/manned examination
claims.claim: The next step of his project would be sending a probe, robotic rover, or manned mission to closely examine the most promising candidate structures.
claims.rationale: stated intent at the same timestamp (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Compton-Belkovich 20x heat output
claims.claim: There is a location on the far side of the Moon, between two craters called Compton and Belkovich, that NASA infrared imaging shows is emitting 20 times the average heat output of the rest of the Moon's far side.
claims.rationale: Siegler et al. 2023: ~180 mW/m² peak, ~20x average highlands; sensor is microwave radiometry, not IR (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: High thorium/uranium concentration
claims.claim: This Compton-Belkovich area has an anomalously high concentration of thorium and (he believes) uranium — radioactive elements.
claims.rationale: LP GRS 5.3 µg/g vs 0–2 background, modeled source 40–55 ppm; U inferred via KREEP association (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Anomalously glassy and reflective
claims.claim: This area is anomalously glassy and highly reflective compared to the rest of the far side of the Moon.
claims.rationale: Jolliff 2011: reflectance 20–40% higher, silica/alkali-feldspar (rhyolitic) signature; 'glassy' loose but compatible (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Anomalously low crater count
claims.claim: NASA scientists analyzed the cratering of this area and concluded the crater count is anomalously low, indicating a much younger age than the rest of the Moon's far side.
claims.rationale: low small-crater density is real, but the authors caveat it as degradation/pyroclastic blanketing, not youth (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Estimated hundreds of millions of years old
claims.claim: Based on standard lunar-geology cratering-rate dating techniques, this area is estimated to be on the order of hundreds of millions of years old, versus 3+ billion years for the rest of the far side.
claims.rationale: peer-reviewed age is ~3.5 Ga (bracketed 1–3.6 Ga), not hundreds of millions; the Copernican count was preliminary (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Granite-block hypothesis for the heat
claims.claim: The best explanation NASA and the planetary science community have come up with for the heat anomaly is a massive ~50-kilometer-wide block of granite beneath the Moon's surface storing heat from billions of years ago.
claims.rationale: Siegler 2023: an ~50 km granitic batholith best explains the hot source (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: Researchers admit granite wouldn't make sense
claims.claim: The researchers who proposed the granite-block hypothesis admit it would not otherwise make geological sense, because granite formation requires large amounts of water and tectonic activity, which the Moon (in the standard picture) never had.
claims.rationale: researchers state granite normally needs water plus plate tectonics, both absent on the Moon (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: No GPR has found the granite block
claims.claim: No ground-penetrating radar imaging has found a granite block of this kind at the site.
claims.rationale: literal but misleading - no GPR detection at CBVC; it was found via microwave radiometry, and GPR was neither attempted nor expected (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: No comparable granite elsewhere in the solar system
claims.claim: Nothing resembling that quantity of granite has been found anywhere else in the solar system.
claims.rationale: Nature: granites are 'nearly absent in the Solar System outside of Earth' (see findings/wave3/geology-remainder.md)

claims.title: NASA plan for a lunar nuclear reactor
claims.claim: NASA has stated there is a plan to build a nuclear reactor on the Moon to power a planned moon base.
claims.rationale: NASA/DOE Fission Surface Power program targets a lunar reactor ~2030 (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Aristarchus anomalously bright crater
claims.claim: There is an anomalously bright crater on the Moon called Aristarchus.
claims.rationale: brightest large crater on the near side; mundane cause is young, fresh, silica-rich material (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: German astronomers saw Aristarchus unusually bright
claims.claim: Astronomers in Germany saw the Aristarchus crater as unusually bright (historical observation).
claims.rationale: Pruss & Witte, Bochum, reported a 5-7 s brightening July 19, 1969 (Crotts citing Cameron 1978) (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Mission Control asked Apollo 11 about Aristarchus
claims.claim: Mission Control told Apollo 11 about the Aristarchus brightness while the crew was in lunar orbit before landing.
claims.rationale: CapCom transcript verbatim at 076:57:07 (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Crew asked to look at Aristarchus from orbit
claims.claim: Apollo 11 crew were asked to look at Aristarchus from orbit around the Moon.
claims.rationale: same exchange asks the crew to look (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Crew reported it "fluorescing"
claims.claim: Armstrong, Aldrin, and Collins looked at Aristarchus and reported: "Yeah, it looks unusually bright, almost like fluorescing. We can definitely see that."
claims.rationale: substance real but the quote is inflated; Armstrong and Aldrin both hedged (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Aristarchus a candidate Apollo 18 landing site
claims.claim: Aristarchus was considered as a potential landing site for Apollo 18, which never flew as a mission.
claims.rationale: Aristarchus Plateau on NASA candidate lists for the canceled late Apollo missions (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Aristarchus in multiple NASA TLP studies
claims.claim: Aristarchus appears in multiple NASA studies of transient lunar phenomena (TLP).
claims.rationale: NASA TR R-277 (1968) and Cameron NSSDC catalog (1978) (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: NASA's centuries-spanning TLP archive
claims.claim: NASA maintains an archive of transient lunar phenomena reports dating back hundreds of years from amateur and professional astronomers.
claims.rationale: NASA published centuries-spanning catalogs; 'maintains' overstates (no living archive) (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Half of TLP events attributed to Aristarchus
claims.claim: About half of the identified TLP events in NASA's archive have been attributed to Aristarchus.
claims.rationale: Crotts: roughly 50% of TLP reports from Aristarchus and vicinity, with observer-bias caveats (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Anomalous radon at Aristarchus
claims.claim: NASA/researchers have detected anomalous quantities of radon at/near Aristarchus.
claims.rationale: radon detected by Apollo 15 and Lunar Prospector alpha spectrometers (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Bright in visible and ultraviolet
claims.claim: Aristarchus is anomalously bright in both the visible and ultraviolet spectra.
claims.rationale: visible confirmed; 'anomalously' bright in UV is interpretive (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Occasional flashes of light
claims.claim: Aristarchus produces occasional flashes of light.
claims.rationale: reports exist in catalogs; physical reality of individual events unproven (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Anomalous color changes and haze
claims.claim: Aristarchus changes color in anomalous ways and becomes hazy in anomalous ways.
claims.rationale: reported repeatedly, never instrumentally confirmed as anomalous (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Potential cave-like entrances at Aristarchus
claims.claim: Some lunar anomalies researchers have identified potential cave-like entrances at the base of Aristarchus.
claims.rationale: no peer-reviewed pit/skylight identified at Aristarchus (confirmed pits are elsewhere) (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: No rover ever sent to Aristarchus
claims.claim: No rover has ever been sent to Aristarchus.
claims.rationale: no soft-landed mission has ever visited the Aristarchus plateau (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Moon "rang like a bell" after booster impacts
claims.claim: During Apollo 11 and 12, the Moon "rang like a bell" when instruments detected seismic signals, and NASA intentionally crashed a booster into the Moon, causing it to ring even longer.
claims.rationale: event real (55-min Apollo 12 signal; longer S-IVB reverberations from Apollo 13 on) - but the same 1970 papers explain it via dry, high-Q, scattering rock; hollow implication debunked (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: MacDonald: "the Moon makes sense... if it's somewhat hollow"
claims.claim: Gordon MacDonald, described as Eisenhower's space advisor, said "The only way in which the Moon makes sense is if it's somewhat hollow."
claims.rationale: quote circulates only through hollow-Moon books; his 1962 JGR paper argues no such thing; 'Eisenhower's advisor' false; hollow Moon itself debunked (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Moon is "bone dry"
claims.claim: The Moon is "bone dry" except for a small amount of water ice at the poles and microscopic amounts of water elsewhere.
claims.rationale: accurate to first order given the claim's own caveats (polar ice, ppm-level water) (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: GRAIL imaged the subsurface via gravity
claims.claim: NASA used a probe called GRAIL to image the subsurface of the Moon by measuring changes in the Moon's gravitational field.
claims.rationale: GRAIL was a twin-spacecraft gravity mapper of the lunar interior (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: GRAIL shows massive subsurface caves
claims.claim: GRAIL data show massive caves and caverns beneath the lunar surface, potentially extending kilometers deep, irregularly distributed.
claims.rationale: GRAIL found candidate mass deficits consistent with empty lava tubes - model-dependent inference, not imaged caves (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Lava tube big enough for "Manhattan and the boroughs"
claims.claim: One cave feature is connected to a giant lava tube large enough to fit "Manhattan and the boroughs" inside it, and roughly "nine kilometers tall."
claims.rationale: real basis is a Philadelphia-scale Marius Hills tube candidate; '9 km tall' matches nothing published (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Zulu "pre-moon society" myths
claims.claim: There are Zulu myths referencing a "pre-moon society," implying the Moon appeared at some point rather than always existing.
claims.rationale: traces to Credo Mutwa's modern writings, not attested ethnography (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Quran passage: "the moon opens up"
claims.claim: The Quran contains a passage referencing "the moon opens up."
claims.rationale: Quran 54:1 'the moon was split'; theological, not structural (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Moon tidally locked, far side unseen
claims.claim: The Moon is tidally locked to the Earth such that the far side is never seen from Earth.
claims.rationale: synchronous rotation per NASA (libration caveat: ~59% visible over time) (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Phobos and Deimos tidally locked to Mars
claims.claim: Phobos and Deimos, the moons of Mars, are tidally locked to Mars.
claims.rationale: textbook tidal locking, the default fate of close-in moons (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Moon unusually large relative to Earth
claims.claim: Earth's Moon is unusually large relative to its parent planet compared to other moon-planet pairs.
claims.rationale: genuine oddity - and the core explanandum of the giant-impact hypothesis (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Giant-impact (Theia) origin theory
claims.claim: The leading scientific explanation for the Moon's formation is a "glancing blow" collision between Earth and a Mars-sized planetoid roughly four billion years ago (giant-impact/Theia hypothesis).
claims.rationale: leading hypothesis, ~4.5 Gya (speaker said ~4); actively refined, normal science (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Anomalous subsurface mass distribution
claims.claim: The distribution of mass below the lunar surface is anomalous, including areas of large mass concentrations (mascons) and areas of large mass deficits (gaps).
claims.rationale: GRAIL mascon bulls-eye surplus ringed by deficits; explained impact physics (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Apollo orbit corrections due to gravity anomalies
claims.claim: Apollo spacecraft orbiting the Moon experienced landing/orbit problems and had to correct orbits due to lunar gravitational anomalies (uneven gravity from mass concentrations).
claims.rationale: mascons discovered 1968 via orbit perturbations; Apollo planners corrected for them (see findings/moon-geology.md)

claims.title: Crick's "Life Itself" (1981) on directed panspermia
claims.claim: Francis Crick wrote a book titled "Life Itself" (1981) about directed panspermia.

claims.title: Crick also wrote a directed-panspermia paper
claims.claim: Francis Crick also wrote a paper about directed panspermia.

claims.title: Mars had an Earth-like atmosphere ~3 Gya
claims.claim: Mars had an Earth-like atmosphere for over a billion years, according to NASA's own studies, roughly three billion years ago.

claims.title: Villarreal at Stockholm University
claims.claim: Beatrice Villarreal is at Stockholm University.
claims.rationale: Villarroel is at Nordita, KTH & Stockholm University (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: 10,000+ transients/year on Palomar/Mount Wilson plates
claims.claim: Villarreal found 10,000-plus "transients" per year for eight years (1949-1957) — light-reflecting, mirror-like/metallic-seeming objects — on photographic plates from the Palomar Observatory / Mount Wilson Observatory.
claims.rationale: ~107,875 automated candidates 1949-57 is real, but POSS-I/Palomar only, mostly unvalidated; 'mirror-like/metallic' is interpretation (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: Period was before Sputnik
claims.claim: This period was before Sputnik was put into space.
claims.rationale: dataset ends 4/28/57; Sputnik launched 10/4/57 (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: NASA calls them "uncorrelated targets"
claims.claim: Villarreal said she spoke to NASA about these transients, and NASA told her they call them "uncorrelated targets."

claims.title: Space Force tracks "uncorrelated targets"
claims.claim: Someone told Villarreal that Space Force tracks these "uncorrelated targets."
claims.rationale: unverifiable conversational claim (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: Militaries remove uncorrelated targets from counts
claims.claim: Militaries remove the "uncorrelated targets" background from the total count of tracked objects in space in order to calculate the true count; this removal uses classified lists compiled by militaries.
claims.rationale: the public satellite catalog does exclude classified objects; the 'subtract' framing is garbled (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: Transients 68% likelier within 24h of a detonation
claims.claim: Villarreal's study found the transients are 68% more likely to appear within 24 hours of a nuclear detonation.

claims.title: Hastings on UFOs at nuclear weapons bases
claims.claim: Michels cites Robert Hastings' work documenting UFOs at nuclear weapons bases across the US.
claims.rationale: Hastings' UFOs & Nukes corpus exists (type A); underlying incidents contested (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: PRP requires reporting even ibuprofen
claims.claim: Personnel with access to sensitive nuclear material are on the "PRP program" (personnel reliability program), which requires reporting things like taking ibuprofen.
claims.rationale: DoDM 5210.42 medication-review requirement plus established service practice (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: Personnel report "Tic Tac saucers" at weapons
claims.claim: Such personnel report seeing "Tic Tac saucers" messing with the nuclear weapons.
claims.rationale: veterans do make such reports (type A); veracity of the events contested (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: Hastings documented 167 whistleblowers
claims.claim: Robert Hastings has documented 167 such whistleblowers.
claims.rationale: Hastings verbatim: 167 veterans interviewed ('whistleblowers' overstates) (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: Villarreal working with a Vanderbilt statistician
claims.claim: Villarreal is working with a statistician at Vanderbilt, "Dr. Steven Brule" (sp?), doing statistical analysis of her data.
claims.rationale: Stephen Bruehl, Vanderbilt University Medical Center, first author doing the statistics (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: Hossenfelder and Keating: "we don't know how to explain this"
claims.claim: Sabina Hossenfelder and Brian Keating have publicly said "we don't know how to explain this" regarding Villarreal's findings.
claims.rationale: both engaged seriously and publicly; the joint verbatim quote was not found (see findings/villarreal.md)

claims.title: German colleague "Ivo Busko" (sp?)
claims.claim: Villarreal updated the public that a colleague of hers in Germany, named "Ivo Busko" (sp?), has extensive astronomical/space experience.

claims.rationale: White's DARPA-funded custom Casimir-cavity work and Casimir Inc. exist (see findings/warp-parapsych.md)

claims.title: Casimir device outputs ~1.5 kilovolt
claims.claim: Sunny White's Casimir device produces something like a "one point five kilovolt" (or some very low voltage) chip output.
claims.rationale: real announced target is 1.5 volts (not kilovolts) at microamps; unreplicated vendor claim (see findings/warp-parapsych.md)

claims.title: GR allows warp drives in principle
claims.claim: General relativity ("Einstein's theory of gravity") allows warp drives in principle.
claims.rationale: an exact GR solution given exotic matter that may not exist in the required quantities (see findings/warp-parapsych.md)

claims.title: Open question: how quantum fluctuations gravitate
claims.claim: An open question in physics is how quantum/zero-point fluctuations gravitate and influence the space-time metric — an area of active research without a consistent theory yet.
claims.rationale: semiclassical gravity/backreaction is a genuine open research area (see findings/warp-parapsych.md)

claims.title: Quantum fields might destabilize warp space-times
claims.claim: One possibility is that how quantum fields gravitate could destabilize warp drive space-times and make them unworkable.
claims.rationale: Finazzi, Liberati & Barcelo 2009: superluminal warp drives are semiclassically unstable (see findings/warp-parapsych.md)

claims.title: Alcubierre requires no break from relativity
claims.claim: The Alcubierre warp drive concept does not require any break from Einstein's relativity — it is consistent with general relativity.
claims.rationale: at the metric level; superluminal bubbles still generically permit closed timelike curves (see findings/warp-parapsych.md)

claims.title: Puthoff coined "space-time metric engineering"
claims.claim: The phrase "space-time metric engineering" was coined by Hal Puthoff.
claims.rationale: the phrase is Puthoff's signature usage since 1996; literal first coinage unprovable (see findings/warp-parapsych.md)

claims.title: Puthoff has written papers on the concept
claims.claim: Hal Puthoff has written papers using/developing the space-time metric engineering concept.
claims.rationale: Physics Essays 1996; JBIS 2002 and 2010 papers exist (see findings/warp-parapsych.md)

claims.title: Davis has written warp/wormhole papers
claims.claim: Eric Davis has written a number of papers on warp drives and traversable wormholes.
claims.rationale: DIA DIRD and STAIF/AIAA papers exist as documents; scientific standing marginal (see findings/warp-parapsych.md)

claims.title: Derakhshani building a new gravitation framework
claims.claim: Derakhshani has studied Puthoff's and Davis's work and is building a new framework to describe how quantum fields gravitate, potentially addressing warp drive feasibility.
claims.rationale: self-description; his published record is adjacent but no warp-feasibility paper found (see findings/warp-parapsych.md)

claims.title: Michels asks if Derakhshani was asked to join
claims.claim: Michels asks Derakhshani if he's ever been asked to be part of "the Legacy UFO program."
claims.rationale: podcast-internal exchange (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Derakhshani has not been asked to join
claims.claim: He has not been asked to join the Legacy program.
claims.rationale: podcast-internal exchange (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Asked Puthoff and Davis how one would join
claims.claim: He once asked Hal Puthoff and Eric Davis how one would go about joining such a program.
claims.rationale: said on the podcast; underlying content is hearsay (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: The described recruitment path
claims.claim: Puthoff and Davis told him the path would be: apply to a major aerospace corporation implicated in the Legacy program, work there a few years on a public project, obtain top-secret SCI clearance, express interest in the Legacy program, and wait for an internal call to applicants or be reached out to.
claims.rationale: described path is indistinguishable from ordinary SAP hiring into an unestablished program (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Discussion with Davis and Weinstein
claims.claim: Michels describes a discussion he had with Eric Davis and Eric Weinstein.
claims.rationale: the Davis/Weinstein discussion exists - it is Michels' own American Alchemy episode, not an independent source (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Davis: no theoretical physicists on "the program" except maybe Haisch
claims.claim: In that discussion, Eric Davis said none of the people on "the program" were theoretical physicists, possibly except one guy, Bernard Haisch.
claims.rationale: as 'Davis said it' (matches the episode's theme; Haisch attribution not transcript-verified); as fact, unfalsifiable (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Puthoff asked by the Bush administration to study disclosure
claims.claim: Hal Puthoff has mentioned he was asked by the (second) Bush administration to partake in a study/review about what it would take for UFO disclosure to occur, including costs and benefits.
claims.rationale: as 'Puthoff has said it'; the study's existence unsupported (no document or second participant) (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Review found proprietary incentives against sharing
claims.claim: That review's conclusions included that each aerospace company wants to keep its progress/work proprietary and doesn't want to reveal secrets to other companies, creating an incentive not to share findings and to be guarded about who is let into the program.
claims.rationale: conclusions of an unverifiable study (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: "The Kingman craft" held by Lockheed
claims.claim: References "the Kingman craft" allegedly held by Lockheed, from Arizona, described as being in a warehouse with "no seams, no rivets."
claims.rationale: one 1973 single-witness affidavit; the Lockheed custody detail has no traceable source at all (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Teller possibly involved in the Legacy program
claims.claim: Derakhshani vaguely recalls suggestions that Edward Teller may have been one of the physicists involved in the (presumed) Legacy program.
claims.rationale: vague recollection of 'suggestions' (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Teller "for sure" on the program if one exists
claims.claim: Edward Teller was on the UFO legacy program "for sure" if one exists.
claims.rationale: 'for sure, if one exists' by its own construction (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Teller's name on a Project Sign/Grudge document
claims.claim: A "Project Sign or Grudge" document exists from pre-Blue Book, the late 1940s, with Edward Teller's name on it, engaging in a UFO review.
claims.rationale: a real 1949 Los Alamos conference transcript with Teller participating; 'Sign or Grudge document' is a mislabel (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Teller got Bob Lazar his EG&G job
claims.claim: Edward Teller got Bob Lazar his job with EG&G.
claims.rationale: Lazar-only claim; peripheral facts check out; Teller never confirmed, no document (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Teller shown Townsend Brown's precipitator demo
claims.claim: Edward Teller was friendly with Thomas Townsend Brown and was shown a demo of Brown's "famed precipitator experiment."
claims.rationale: family lore supports a 1967 Brown-visits-Teller demo-fan meeting; 'friendly' and 'precipitator' are embellishments (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Teller: "I have no idea how this works"
claims.claim: Teller reportedly said "I have no idea how this works" and "freaks out" after seeing the Townsend Brown demo.
claims.rationale: the quote appears in no locatable source (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Odlum (Northrop) invested in Townsend Brown
claims.claim: Floyd Odlum — described as majority/one of the biggest shareholders in Northrop (pre-merger with Grumman) — invested in Townsend Brown's work.
claims.rationale: Odlum-ranch interest appears in the same lore, but Atlas Corp controlled Convair, not Northrop (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Teller associated with Lawrence Livermore Lab
claims.claim: Edward Teller was "very obviously deeply associated with" Lawrence Livermore Lab.
claims.rationale: Teller co-founded and directed Livermore (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: A letter in which Teller mentions John Alexander
claims.claim: There is a letter in which Teller discusses/mentions John Alexander.
claims.rationale: relationship confirmed (Alexander's own site; 1993 conference); the letter itself not publicly locatable (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Alexander synonymous with govt-side UFO research
claims.claim: John Alexander is described as synonymous with UFO research on the government side for the last seventy years.
claims.rationale: ~40 years by his own account, not seventy; 'synonymous' is promotional inflation (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Letter commending Alexander on non-lethal warfare
claims.claim: There is a letter where Teller commends John Alexander for making "important updates in non-lethal warfare."
claims.rationale: same status as C429, pending the document (see findings/secret-programs.md)

claims.title: Inside the Renaissance Technologies campus
claims.claim: Derakhshani has been inside the Renaissance Technologies campus a couple of times as an undergraduate for lectures/colloquiums.
claims.rationale: the RenTech campus near Stony Brook and its seminar culture are documented; the specific attendance is self-reported (see findings/wave3/people-remainder.md)

claims.title: Spoke to Jim Simons as an undergrad
claims.claim: Derakhshani spoke to Jim Simons a couple of times while Simons was alive, when Derakhshani was an undergrad.
claims.rationale: Simons' Stony Brook role and accessibility are multiply confirmed; the specific conversations are self-reported (see findings/wave3/people-remainder.md)

claims.title: No UFO interest among the Stony Brook physicists
claims.claim: Derakhshani never came across any hint of interest in UFOs among Stony Brook mathematicians/physicists he interacted with.
claims.rationale: a personal-experience negative that can't be checked from outside; consistent with a mainstream-department baseline (see findings/wave3/people-remainder.md)

claims.title: Medallion Fund's 30% returns since 1989
claims.claim: Renaissance Technologies' Medallion Fund has made "thirty percent year-over-year return" since 1989.
claims.rationale: real figures are ~66% gross / 39% net since 1988, not 30% since 1989; the qualitative point holds (see findings/wave3/people-remainder.md)

claims.title: Medallion Fund grew past $100 billion
claims.claim: The Medallion Fund grew to over "a hundred billion dollars" plus.
claims.rationale: the >$100B is cumulative trading gains, not fund AUM; Medallion is employee-only and closed since 1993 (see findings/wave3/people-remainder.md)

claims.title: Brookhaven's Cosmotron the "largest accelerator in the US"
claims.claim: Brookhaven National Labs hosts the Cosmotron, described as "the largest particle accelerator in the US."
claims.rationale: with caveat - BNL: the Cosmotron was the world's highest-energy accelerator at 3.3 GeV in 1953; superseded by the Bevatron (1954), dismantled 1969 (see findings/wave3/people-remainder.md)
